title: Underlying cohomology comparison for K-flat scalar extension
statement: Let a:X→T be any scheme morphism, f:A→B any map of commutative rings, and P a K-flat cochain complex of intrinsic modules over the constant ring A_T [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let D be any prescribed cochain universal model of derived extension along f, with independently chosen source and target localization universes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let L be the restricted regular B_T-module in degree zero, and compute the intrinsic tensor P tensor L using P itself [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For each integer q, the underlying set sheaves of a_B^* H^q(D.T(QP)) and a_A^* H^q(P tensor L) are isomorphic [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. No finiteness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: The K-flat counit computes derived extension by the actual termwise ordinary extension. Its objects and maps are specified by the cochain model.

The proved independent-coefficient underlying tensor comparison identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of extension of M with Res(B_T) tensor M, naturally in M. Compose its components with D.obj_eq; use D.map_eq for naturality. Symmetry exchanges the factors. The tensor-with-single-complex isomorphism identifies the resulting termwise tensor with the intrinsic total tensor P tensor L.

Apply the exact underlying-abelian-sheaf functors to the cochain comparison. Their homology comparison and the two localization/homology factorizations identify underlying cohomology. The source-derived universe is independent of the standard universe of the tensor, because both compare with ordinary cochain homology.

For either coefficient ring the canonical coefficient map is invertible. The scalar-extension ring-isomorphism theorem identifies its final scalar extension with restriction along the inverse, preserving the underlying sheaf. Compare the original and independent-coefficient scalar-extension presheaves by the identity on pure tensors. The existing unit-normalized underlying-set inverse-image identification then identifies module pullback with set inverse image. Apply set inverse image to the preceding cohomology isomorphism and compose.

theorem restrictedScalarTensorCohomologyComparison
    {T X : Scheme.{u}} (a : X ⟶ T)
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T B))]
    (D : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.{u + 1, u, u + 1, wA, wB}
      (restrictedScalarRingMap T f))
    (P : CochainComplex (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T A)) ℤ)
    (hP : P.IsAcyclicTensorKFlat) (q : ℤ) :
    Nonempty
      (((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
        (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
          (proEtaleConstantModulePullback a B
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
              (proEtaleRingModules T (proEtaleConstantRing T B)) q).obj
                (D.T.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)))))) ≅
      ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
        (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj
          (proEtaleConstantModulePullback a A
            (restrictedScalarTensorCohomology T f P hP q)))))
